import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the event invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {title} - Invitation

{title}

Date: {date}

{description}

Notes: {notes}

""" def generate_event_invite(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The name or title of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain multiple lines and formatting). date : str The scheduled date for the event. notes : str Extra information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A fully sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Validate input types for name, value in (("title", title), ("description", description), ("date", date), ("notes", notes)): if not isinstance(value, str): raise TypeError(f"Argument '{name}' must be a string, got {type(value).__name__}") # Escape all user-provided content to prevent XSS escaped_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") escaped_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) escaped_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Format the invitation using the predefined template html_invite = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( title=escaped_title, description=escaped_description, date=escaped_date, notes=escaped_notes ) return html_invite
